data.name: Navjot
data.gender_notes: Navjot is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nav means new and Jot means victory. This name is derived from the Sanskrit language and is rooted in Hindu mythology. The name Navjot carries the meaning “New Victory” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Navjot usually hope their child will grow to embody new victory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the triumph of the spirit over the material world.
data.etymology: Navjot belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “New Victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Navjot total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Navjot holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, especially among the Sikh community. According to the Hindu calendar, the nine auspicious days leading up to the new moon are collectively referred to as Navratri. Navjot could be interpreted as the embodiment of this concept; someone who brings new victories or successes with each passing day or new beginning. It is a powerful, positive name that conveys renewal and progress.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Navjot can be traced back to Hinduism and particularly to the concept of Divine Creativity. The name Navjot is deeply intertwined with the concept of Benevolent Goddess Shakti, who is worshipped during Navratri. The name signifies that with the grace and blessings of the Divine Mother, one can conquer their inner demons, overcome challenges, and enjoy spiritual victories throughout their life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Navjot: New Beginning, Radiant Light. This name signifies the inner light that guides one through new beginnings and challenges in life. It is a reminder of the divine light within, always illuminating the path towards growth and transformation.

Navjot was a prominent sage and philosopher in ancient India, known for his contributions to the Bhagavad Gita.
Time period: 5th century BCE
Context: Navjot is believed to have been the sage Vyasa's disciple and the one to whom the Bhagavad Gita was revealed.

Navjot Singh Sidhu is a popular Indian politician and former cricket player. He was born on October 20, 1963, in the Indian state of Punjab.
Time period: Late 20th century
Context: Navjot Singh Sidhu gained fame as a cricket player, particularly for his match-winning performances in the 1983 and 1992 Cricket World Cups. After retiring from cricket, he entered politics and has been a member of various political parties in India.
